comment: Provenance for third-party assets that MicroDraw used to fetch from a CDN at
runtime and now ships locally. Run `npm run verify-vendor` to check that every
file still matches the bytes that were downloaded, and to see the exact URL to
re-download from when bumping a version.
Loaded by app/public/js/microdraw.js (scripts), the mustache views (font) and the example pages in app/public/examples/ (Vue 2, Vue.Draggable).

assets.name: codeflask
assets.note: Was requested unpinned as unpkg.com/codeflask/build/codeflask.min.js, so the version served could change at any time. 1.4.1 is what that URL resolved to on the retrieval date; the versions loaded before then are not recoverable.

assets.name: Openseadragon-screenshot
assets.note: Kept under its own filename because it is NOT identical to the openseadragonScreenshot.js already in that directory: the CDN build adds a viewer.screenshotInstance.showOptions guard. The suffixed name preserves both.

assets.name: roboto-100-latin
assets.note: URL taken from https://fonts.googleapis.com/css?family=Roboto:100 requested with a Chrome user agent, which is what selects the woff2 subsets. gstatic re-subsets its binaries at the same versioned URL — hours after retrieval it served 7816 bytes where this copy is 16140 — so the checksum guards this file against in-repo drift but cannot be reproduced by re-downloading. That instability is itself the reason to vendor the font: otherwise the glyphs behind the reference screenshots could change without notice.

assets.name: roboto-100-latin-ext
assets.note: Same gstatic re-subsetting caveat as roboto-100-latin.

assets.name: vue
assets.note: Development build, used only by app/public/examples/composer.html and composer-0.html (M8b, retrieved 2026-10-13). They requested it unpinned as cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/vue/dist/vue.js, which on that date served these exact bytes (Vue 2.7.16, the last Vue 2): the pages are Vue 2 code (new Vue, v-for with v-if).

assets.name: vuedraggable
assets.note: Used only by the example composer pages (M8b, retrieved 2026-10-13), same URL as before. It expects window.Sortable (sortablejs) when a <draggable> is mounted; the pages register the component but their <draggable> markup is commented out, and Sortable was never loaded, so it is not vendored.

derived.note: Hand-written from the Google Fonts stylesheet: only the latin and latin-ext @font-face blocks are kept (the app renders Latin text only) and their src URLs point at the local woff2 files. Not byte-identical to any upstream file, so it is not checksummed.
